title: Find out whether a clip on a locked track can still be deleted
goal: Locking a track is a promise that nothing on it changes. On the timeline the lock holds: its clips cannot be clicked, dragged, split or ripple deleted. But the plain delete path checks only whether the layer itself is locked, not its track, so a clip on a locked track that gets picked some other way (on the canvas, from Layers, by Select All) may still be deleted by Delete or Command Delete. Find out, and if it does, make the lock hold against every delete.
notes: Manager pass 2026-10-05, from reading the code, NOT reproduced (the loop held the probe). PhotonzCore/Document.swift:687-689 deletableLayerIDs filters on layer.isLocked only; Track.isLocked lives in DocumentTracks.swift:52. EditorState+Layout.swift:48-56 deleteSelectedLayers uses actionableLayerIDs then deleteLayers. canDeleteClipPieceInHand (EditorState+ClipBar.swift:155-161) has no track-lock check either. Timeline-side guards that DO hold: EditorState+ClipBar.swift:111-113, 357-361; EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:77-87, 327; TimelineMenuEdits.swift:58-91. Whether a locked track's clip can be picked on the canvas at all is the first thing to learn; if it cannot, this is likely a no-op.
acceptance: Reproduce at Next defaults before changing anything: lock V1 on a recording, pick its clip by clicking the picture on the canvas, press Delete and then Command Delete, and also try Select All then Delete; write what happened in this task's log with the walk or steps used
If the clip survives every way, record that, add a walk that proves it, and close the task with no app change

If any way deletes it: deletableLayerIDs (and every delete path that does not go through it) leaves out a layer on a locked track, the Delete Layer row greys out when that is all that is picked, and a unit test in PhotonzCore is written first for each path
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: REPRODUCED at Next defaults (no flags): walk /tmp/lt/explore.json = openSampleRecording, pause, seek quarter, hover Track V1, press 'Track V1 Lock', click the picture at (640,300), key delete. describe before: layers 1, V1 lock lit + lane striped (1-locked-clicked-sc.png); after delete: layers 0, the whole recording gone, black canvas, V1 empty (2-after-delete-sc.png). The clip CAN be picked on the canvas while its track is locked, and Delete takes it.

Fix: PhotonzCore deletableLayerIDs now also leaves out every layer on a locked track (layerIDsOnLockedTracks, one layout per call), so canDeleteLayers/Delete Layer row greys when only such a clip is picked; removeClipPiece (and so rippleDeleteClipPiece) refuses a clip on a locked track. App: deleteLayer(id:) and Cut read canDeleteLayers instead of the layer's own lock; canDeleteClipPieceInHand checks isClipLocked. Tests first: DeletableLayersTests.clipsOnALockedTrackAreNotDeletable, whatIsInsideAClipOnALockedTrackIsNotDeletable, TimelineMenuEditsTests.pieceOnALockedTrackStays (failed 7 issues before, pass after). Full suite 11385 tests green. New walk a-locked-track-keeps-its-clip-walk (no flags): Delete key, Delete Layer (log: 'menu row dimmed, nothing deleted'), Cmd-Delete, Cut, whole-canvas marquee + Delete all keep the recording (layers 2); rectangle + locked recording picked together, Delete takes only the rectangle (layers 1). Select All has no walk stand-in, so the marquee tool draws the same whole-canvas region. Also green: 6 other *locked* walks, delete-key-drops-a-timeline-piece, trim-with-pieces, tracks-you-can-add-rename-group.

left rough (no task, does not clear the bar): deleting a locked TRACK itself from its header (deleteTracksInHand) still takes the track and its clips. That is a deliberate whole-track act and Premiere allows deleting a locked track too, so left as is; not reproduced as a complaint. Collage/merge-down also remove layers without a track-lock check, but they are still-image edits that do not reach a recording's clip. No audit written: a bug fix with no new surface to playtest.
